until.description: Only commits whose git committer time is at or before this RFC 3339 timestamp, such as 2026-08-31T23:59:59Z. The bound is inclusive. Combined with since and the email filters, a commit must match every filter that is set.

tools.description: Create a pull request from an already-pushed branch. To stack it, pass parentPullNumber: the base becomes that pull request's head branch (any other base is rejected), and head must have been built on that branch, meaning the two share a commit beyond the parent's own base. A head built off trunk or from unrelated history is rejected with the rebase to run. A head that has since fallen behind the parent is accepted and the response carries needsRestack, because the pull request cannot land until it is restacked; this tool never restacks. stackParent is the stored parent's number, read back after the create.

tools.description: Update a pull request's title, description, and lifecycle through the public fields. Omit title or body to leave that field unchanged; pass an empty body to clear the description. Lifecycle is state (open or closed) plus draft, sent independently: state closed closes and ignores draft; state open reopens, and without draft true marks ready and publishes an existing draft; draft true reopens as a draft, alone or together with state open; draft false marks ready and reopens a closed pull request. Send one lifecycle field, both, or neither, so a metadata-only update is valid. Metadata and lifecycle together send one public UpdatePullRequest. Origin applies present fields in its documented order; a failure can leave some fields applied, so re-read after an error. merged is not writable, and ready is draft false or state open rather than a state value.

tools.description: Retarget a pull request's base branch, stack it on another pull request, or move it off its stack. With parentPullNumber, the base becomes that pull request's head branch and the stack parent is set in the same update. With base, the pull request is retargeted to that branch: the head branch of an open pull request makes that pull request the parent, and the default branch or a branch with no open pull request moves it off its stack. Stacking is allowed only when this pull request's branch was built on the parent, meaning the two share a commit beyond the parent's own base; a branch built off trunk or from unrelated history is rejected with the rebase to run. A branch that has fallen behind the parent is accepted and the response carries needsRestack, because the pull request cannot land until it is restacked. This tool stacks and unstacks but never restacks: no commit is rebased or replayed. Returns the stored base and head refs, plus stackParent when stacked.

parentPullNumber.description: Pull request to stack on, by number. Its head branch becomes the base. Send this or base.

tools.description: Merge a pull request, or a stack up to and including it. On a stacked pull request this lands every open pull request from the stack root through this one in one commit (one squash commit with squash, one merge commit otherwise); Origin checks every member first and lands nothing if one is blocked. Where a merge queue owns the branch, a single pull request is queued instead, and nothing lands yet. If Origin queues a stack as one merge queue entry instead, its members land in one commit or none do. When the call queues, mergeCommitSha and mergedPrefix are empty, because nothing has landed yet. To land a stack one pull request at a time, merge the lowest open one each time; each becomes its own commit, and the ones above usually need a restack after each landing. Requires the expected head SHA of this pull request. Optional mergeMethod (merge or squash); omit it and Origin picks a method the repository accepts. mergedPrefix lists every pull request that landed. Pull requests above the target stay open; skippedDescendants is currently always empty.

tools.description: Read a project's research: what=status (everything at a glance), list or record (collection, id), runs, run, summary, evidence (run: what the version expected, what Saturn observed, what the program reported, and three verdicts), samples (run, cursor, limit, only=all|disputed|errors), log (run, stream=stdout|stderr), resources, labels, compare (left and right are version ids), sample_across (sample, runs), events, environment, policy, inside_list, inside (run, sample, model), data_list (every data input, its hash, whether it changed, who read it), data_profile (path, split: rows, columns, missing, common values), data_overlap (left and right are data files, columns, leftSplit, rightSplit: identical rows between two files, exact duplicates only), data_preview (path, split, cursor, limit: the rows themselves), metrics (run, cursor: training metrics a program logged), paired (left and right are {runId, modelId?}, scorer, only=all|improved|regressed|unchanged|missing, sliceField, higherIsBetter: sample by sample, with improvements, regressions, missing samples, slices and an interval only when the two were measured the same way; saves nothing), remote (the SSH host the person configured, and remote runs), session_inside (session: what an inspection session read), artifact (id: a kept output's content, never run), notebook (path: whether its kernel is running and what it ran), import_preview (path, format=jsonl|json|csv|tsv|trainer, columns, scoreColumns: how a JSONL, JSON, CSV or TSV result file would come in, changing nothing), bundle_preview (path: what a project bundle holds and what would conflict, changing nothing).

left.description: For compare, a version id; for paired, {runId, modelId?}.

right.description: For compare, a version id; for paired, {runId, modelId?}.

columns.description: For import_preview: which column holds sampleId, input, output, expected, modelId or category, where it is not named so.

scoreColumns.description: For import_preview: the columns that are scores.

tools.description: Wait for an experiment run to end, up to 600 seconds at a time, and get its status with its summary, or its newest resource readings if it is still going. Call again to keep waiting.

Make or change a research record. Leave out id to make one. Collections: questions (title), hypotheses (title, questionId, made only, never changed), experiments (title, command, cwd, inputs, evaluation, models, seeds, envNames, questionId, hypothesisId), models (source, weightsRevision, name, parentId, referenceId, trainingData, producedBy), findings (text, runIds), counterexamples (runId, sampleId, note). What you write as a finding is recorded as your suggestion. You cannot set a verdict or a label: those are the person's. delete: true with collection experiments, id and expectedRevision moves an imported experiment, its versions and runs to the records' trash; an experiment frozen or run here is the person's to delete, and one that other records still refer to is not moved.

id.description: The record to change. Leave out to make a new one.

expectedRevision.description: The revision of the record you read, when changing one.

delete.description: With collection experiments, id and expectedRevision: move this imported experiment to the trash.

tools.description: Run an experiment. action=freeze (experiment) makes or finds the version holding its code, data and settings as they are in this chat's folder. action=start (version, attempt) starts it and returns at once; a new attempt number runs the same version again. action=stop (run) ends a run.

Set up the project's Python. action=check reports the interpreter, packages and devices. action=create makes .venv (python, withCore, timeoutSeconds). action=install adds a kit (core, interpretability, training, analysis, notebooks), packages, or sync=true from the lock file (timeoutSeconds). action=set chooses an interpreter (python). action=stop ends the job. Create and install run as a job: read what=environment to follow it.

Look inside a model on a run's samples or your own prompts, with the Python the experiment's command starts with. action=activations (runId, sampleId, modelId) reads each layer. action=patch (runId, sampleId, sourceModelId, targetModelId, layer) replaces the residual stream leaving a layer with the source's. action=sweep (runId, sampleIds up to 32, sourceModelId, targetModelId, layers) patches every layer. action=compare (runId, modelId, otherModelId, input, expected) reads two models on a prompt of your own. action=prompts (runId, modelId, clean, corrupted, expected, alternative) restores each layer and position of a corrupted prompt from a clean one with the same number of tokens, beside a random control. action=features (runId, modelId, prompt, layer, and saeRelease with saeId, or saePath; optionally expected, alternative and ablate) reads the residual stream leaving a layer through a sparse autoencoder: the strongest features per token and how well it was rebuilt, and with ablate a feature's id, how the margin moves beside a random feature of similar activation and beside splicing the unmodified reconstruction. A feature has an id, not a name. Results are saved with the run. action=session (modelIds, title, cwd) opens an inspection session for exploring models without a scored run; compare, prompts and features then take sessionId in place of runId and keep their readings with the session.

modelIds.description: For a session: 1 to 32 project models it looks at.

tools.description: Bring evidence in or take it out. action=import (path, format, columns, scoreColumns, evaluation, title, expectedSha256 from the preview) brings a JSONL, JSON, CSV or TSV result file in as a run marked imported: it keeps unknown provenance unknown and never gets an interval of its own; preview it first with research_read what=import_preview. action=bundle_export (path, optional) writes the project's evidence and Markdown and HTML reports as a bundle. action=bundle_import (path) brings a bundle in without overwriting different evidence; preview it with research_read what=bundle_preview. Credentials, permissions and live remote jobs never come with a bundle. action=artifact_register (kind=figure|json|notebook|reference, path or uri, title, runId or inspectionId, metadata) keeps a figure, analysis JSON or notebook snapshot with its hash, or names a large store by reference; nothing in it is run. action=artifacts_from_run (runId) snapshots what the run listed in SATURN_RUN_ARTIFACTS. action=save_counterexamples (the paired fields, only, title) keeps every sample of a paired comparison, regressions by default, as a counterexample set.

Run on the SSH host the person configured in Environment; read it with research_read what=remote. Only the person sets the host. action=check connects and checks Saturn's worker and the working folder there. action=start (version, attempt, timeoutSeconds up to 7 days) runs a frozen version there and returns at once: the job keeps going with Saturn closed, and research_wait follows it as it would a local run. Stop it with research_run action=stop.

Run code in a project notebook's own kernel, with the project's Python. action=start opens the kernel; action=run (cells: each {cell, code}, the cell's id and the code to run, in order) runs them and keeps their outputs; action=interrupt, restart or stop act on the kernel. Read where it stands with research_read what=notebook. Edit the notebook's cells as a file.

Start a task: another agent working on its own in a separate git worktree and branch, while you carry on. Give it everything it needs in the prompt, since it does not see this chat. Its code reaches the project only if the person merges it. A task cannot start another task, and at most 4 run at once.

prompt.description: What the task should do, complete in itself.

tools.description: Follow tasks. what=list shows this project's tasks. what=status (task) says how one stands: its status, what it answered, what it is waiting for, and what it changed. what=wait (task, seconds) holds your turn until it ends or needs a decision, up to 600 seconds at a time. Only the person can answer a task's approval, or merge or discard it.

Delete a task of this project that has ended and whose worktree the person has merged or discarded: its conversation is removed, and no code is lost. A task still going, or one whose worktree is still open, is refused: stopping, merging and discarding are the person's.
